'''Stacey Franklin Jones''' is an American computer scientist, and academic administrator who was the fifth chancellor of [[Elizabeth City State University]] from 2014 to 2015. 

== Life ==
Jones is from [[Boston]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=September 4, 2014 |title=Stacey Franklin Jones Named Chancellor of Elizabeth City State University |url=https://newsroom.ecsu.edu/stacey-franklin-jones-named-chancellor-of-elizabeth-city-state-university/ |access-date=2024-02-15 |website=Elizabeth City State University |language=en-US}}</ref> She earned a B.S. in mathematics, magna cum laude, from [[Howard University]] in 1982.<ref name=":0" /> From 1982 to 1993, she worked in Maryland for [[Northrop Grumman]] as a defense and electronic systems software engineer and [[Product Development Management|product development manager]].<ref name=":0" /> She completed M.S. degrees in numerical science (1986) and [[technical management]] (1991) at [[Johns Hopkins University]]. In 1997, Jones earned a Ph.D. in [[computer science]] from the [[George Washington University]].<ref name=":0" /> Her dissertation was titled, ''Major Cost Categories for a Rough-Order-Magnitude Cost Model for Multimedia Computer-based Training''.<ref name=":3">{{Cite thesis |last=Franklin |first=Stacey Allison |title=Major Cost Categories for a Rough-Order-Magnitude Cost Model for Multimedia Computer-based Training |date=1997 |degree=Ph.D. |publisher=George Washington University |oclc=37600275}}</ref> [[C. Dianne Martin]] was her doctoral advisor.<ref name=":3" />

In 1997, Jones joined the computer science department at Johns Hopkins University as a research scientist and adjunct faculty member.<ref name=":0" /> She joined [[Benedict College]] in 2000 as the chair of the mathematics and computer science department.<ref name=":0" /> She served as its dean of the school of science, technology, engineering and mathematics from 2002 to 2008.<ref name=":0" /> Jones became the vice president of sponsored programs and research in 2007 and senior vice president in 2009.<ref name=":0" /> In July 2010, she became the provost and vice president for academic affairs of [[Bowie State University]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-12-28 |title=Stacey Franklin Jones Resigns as Chancellor of Elizabeth City State University |url=https://www.wiareport.com/2015/12/stacey-franklin-jones-resigns-as-chancellor-of-elizabeth-city-state-university/ |access-date=2024-02-15 |website=Women In Academia Report}}</ref> In the fall of 2011, she returned to the private sector.<ref name=":0" /> On October 1, 2014, Jones became the fifth chancellor and tenth chief executive officer of [[Elizabeth City State University]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2015-12-22 |title=Elizabeth City State Chancellor Announces Resignation |url=https://www.diverseeducation.com/demographics/african-american/article/15097646/elizabeth-city-state-chancellor-announces-resignation |access-date=2024-02-15 |website=Diverse: Issues In Higher Education |language=en-us}}</ref> Succeeding interim chancellor, [[Charles Becton]], she is the first female in the role.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /> Jones resigned on December 31, 2015.<ref name=":1" /> From August 2016 to January 2018, she was the interim provost and vice president for academic affairs at [[Norfolk State University]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Jones |first=Stacey Franklin |date=2018 |title=CV |url=https://www.marshall.edu/provost-search/files/2018/04/Jones-CV.pdf |access-date=2024-02-14 |website=Franklin Marshal University}}</ref> She became the special projects assistant to the interim president in February 2018.<ref name=":2" /> In 2018, she joined [[Fairmont State University]] as its vice president for institutional effectiveness and strategic operations.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr. Stacey Jones joins the University leadership |url=https://www.fairmontstate.edu/news/2018/08/dr-stacey-jones-joins-university-leadership.aspx |access-date=2024-02-15 |website=www.fairmontstate.edu}}</ref>

Jones has two children.<ref name=":0" />
